title: למידין לפני רבי

paragraphs: 'Those who learn before Rabbi,' or 'before the sages,' means Levi (see his entry). Tosafot, Menaḥot (80, end of side b), however, says that 'those who learn before Rabbi' is another sage. Sefer Keritot, Leshon Limmudim, gate 2, §15: in a baraita we find, 'Those who learn before the sages say: Let him bring something that goes entirely to the altar,' Megillah (11)—a scribal error; it should read Me'ilah (9b). Levi said, 'Let him bring something,' etc. It is taught in support of Levi: where has this misappropriated sacred value gone? Those who learn before the sages say, etc., let him bring something, etc. Rashi explains: those who learn before the sages means Levi; he recites it in Rabbi's name. Tosafot there writes: this is not the Levi mentioned in Sanhedrin, for we have not found Levi mentioned in a baraita. Moreover, this is not the method: to bring proof for Levi's words from Levi himself.
